headline: Coast Guard searches off Nantucket for missing medical plane with six aboard
dek: A Canadian-registered air ambulance lost contact with federal flight controllers early Saturday while traveling from Bermuda to Boston, prompting an air-and-sea search south of Nantucket.
body: The U.S. Coast Guard is searching waters off Nantucket for a medical transport aircraft that lost contact with federal flight controllers early Saturday while flying from Bermuda to Boston. The Coast Guard’s Northeast District said in an [official update](https://x.com/USCGNortheast/status/2106332164568801317) that the Gulfstream G100 had six people aboard and that air and surface crews had begun looking for it. The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed to [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/coast-guard-searching-missing-medical-transfer-jet-bound-boston/DLHUFCDJ2FCMBESR4W3MIIOEFA/) that it had lost contact with the flight.

The aircraft departed L.F. Wade International Airport in Bermuda on a flight to Boston Logan International Airport. The FAA issued a search-and-rescue alert at about 1:20 a.m. Saturday, according to [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/medical-plane-missing-nantucket-six-on-board/). CBS reported that the jet took off at about 11:40 p.m. Eastern time Friday and was expected to reach Logan at roughly 1:30 a.m. The plane did not arrive, Massachusetts Port Authority spokesperson Jennifer Mehigan told Boston 25, which said the search area was off Nantucket.

The aircraft was identified as a Gulfstream G-100 with Canadian registration C-GRJP. Boston 25 reported that it is operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, an Ontario-based company that provides medical transfers. The Associated Press said the Canadian-registered jet had four crew members and two passengers when it left Bermuda. Officials have not released the names, ages or medical circumstances of anyone aboard, and those details should not be inferred from the aircraft’s role as an air ambulance.

The response is drawing resources from across the region. Boston 25 reported that the Coast Guard deployed an HC-144 Ocean Sentry aircraft and an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter from Air Station Cape Cod, a 47-foot motor lifeboat crew from Station Brant Point on Nantucket and the Coast Guard cutter William Sparling. [NPR reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/03/nx-s1-5597878/coast-guard-searching-for-missing-medical-plane-carrying-6-people) that the agency also sent an HC-130 Hercules aircraft. The mix of aircraft, boats and a cutter reflects the size of the ocean search area and the need to look from the air and the water.

Local authorities are involved as the search extends beyond the federal crews. The [Martha’s Vineyard Times](https://www.mvtimes.com/2026/10/03/coast-guard-searching-for-missing-plane-off-nantucket/) reported that Nantucket Memorial Airport manager Preston Harimon said the aircraft had reportedly declared an emergency before contact was lost. The airport manager said Coast Guard-led rescue work was underway, while Nantucket police and harbormaster personnel were searching along the island’s south shore. That account adds a ground-and-shore component to a case centered offshore.

The last known circumstances remain incomplete. The Associated Press reported that air-traffic-control audio captured a controller asking whether the pilot was “coming in blind,” then confirming that the pilot had declared an emergency before the communication ended. The pilot’s words were not audible in the recording, and the audio does not establish what caused the emergency. Flight-tracking data reviewed by CBS showed a rapid descent before contact was lost, but that data alone does not explain the aircraft’s condition or location.

The search also has an international dimension. AP reported that four of the six people aboard were Canadian nationals and that Canada’s transport minister said his government was monitoring the response. Bermuda airport operator Skyport told AP that the aircraft had four crew members and two passengers. Bermuda Premier David Burt said, according to CBS, that officials were in contact with families and were hoping all six people would be found safe.

As of the latest agency and public-broadcaster reports reviewed Saturday evening, the Coast Guard had not announced that the plane or any person aboard had been found. The Coast Guard said it would provide updates as they became available, while the National Transportation Safety Board told AP it was gathering information and had no further update at the time of that report. For Nantucket, Cape Cod and Boston, the immediate confirmed story is an active search in nearby waters—not a confirmed crash sequence, casualty count or cause. Those questions remain for investigators and rescuers to establish.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Coast Guard searches for missing medical plane off Nantucket
seoDescription: The Coast Guard is searching off Nantucket for a Canadian-registered medical plane with six people aboard after FAA contact was lost on a Bermuda-to-Boston flight.
